newsitem.title: USA: Dow dismissal from California implant case upheld.
newsitem.headline: Dow dismissal from California implant case upheld.

text.p: Dow Chemical Co. said Thursday the California Court of Appeal here upheld a lower court ruling that dismisses the company from liability in 1,800 silicone breast implant lawsuits.
Dow Chemical, of Midland, Mich., said the decision means that Dow has been dismissed from about 5,000 of the approximately 14,000 cases pending against it.

Dow Chemical and Dow Corning Corp., a joint venture with Corning Inc., have been sued by thousands of women with silicone breast implants who allege the implants have caused medical problems such as connective tissue diseases.

Dow Chemical argues that because it did not develop or manufacture breast implants, it should not be held responsible for their alleged injuries based on its half ownership of Dow Corning. Dow has acknowledged that it conducted industrial worker safety testing of some silicone compounds in the 1940s and 1950s under contract to Dow Corning.

Dow Corning, at one time the world's largest maker of silicone breast implants, froze the thousands of lawsuits it is facing when it filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy protection in May 1995. It denies the claims, saying there is no medical evidence to support the allegations.
In the California case, Dow Chemical and Corning originally were granted a summary judgment dismissing them from the case by Superior Court Judge Robert J. O'Neill on March 21, 1994.

Dow Chemical executives said the ruling from the influential California appellate court, which they received late Wednesday, is a significant one in the ongoing battle over who should be held responsible for the alleged injuries.

"The fact is that Dow Chemical is not now and never has been in any silicone business, including the breast implant business, and should not be in this litigation," John Scriven, general counsel for Dow Chemical, said in a statement.
Plaintiff's attorney Joe Dunn from the Laguna Niguel, Calif., law firm of Robinson, Phillips & Calcagnie, was unavailable for comment.
In May, the appellate division of the New York State Supreme Court upheld a lower court ruling that dismissed Dow Chemical from more than 1,200 implant suits.
Dow Chemical said the majority of the remaining cases against it are under the jurisdiction of U.S. District Court Judge Sam Pointer in Birmingham, Ala.

The company is in the process of appealing an April 1995 decision by Pointer that cleared the way for those cases to be heard by state court juries. Dow Chemical is also facing about 150 cases in the Texas state court system.

The company is also appealing a Nevada jury verdict from October 1995 that ordered the company to pay $14.1 million in damages to a woman who had Dow Corning implants. That verdict was the first case in which Dow Chemical went to trial as a sole defendant in a breast implant case.
Dow Corning was originally named as a co-defendant in the Nevada case. But the bankruptcy court filing removed it from the case.
